content:
After adjusting its computing resource usage policy in May, Google will limit the Gemini models accessible to free users and AI Plus subscribers.

According to support documents updated this week, Gemini App users without a Google AI subscription will only be able to use the (3.5) Flash-Lite model. From October 9, users who do not pay for a Gemini subscription will no longer be able to use (3.6) Flash or (3.1) Pro.

At the same time, AI Plus subscribers will only be able to use Flash-Lite and Flash, with Pro no longer offered. These users, who pay US$4.99 per month, will "receive an email explaining when the changes will take effect".

Gemini Model Google AI Plan Flash-Lite Flash Pro Without a plan ✓ X X AI Plus ✓ ✓ X AI Pro ✓ ✓ ✓ AI Ultra ✓ ✓ ✓

By contrast, AI Pro and AI Ultra users will not see any reduction in their usage quotas. On the contrary, customers paying US$19.99 per month will gain access to the Deep Think option, featuring "maximum parallel reasoning" capabilities — a feature currently limited to plans priced at US$99.99 and US$199.99 per month.

The most-liked comment was posted by Glitter Guru

"Argon had better be able to replace Pro", otherwise I expect to launch 4 Pro alongside Argon at that time. If not, and 3.1 Pro remains the top model for most users, I will cancel my Pro plan.

Using AI Ultra's Gemini 3.1 Pro with Deep Think

The Gemini App also appears to be adding three reasoning intensity options in October — "low", "medium" and "high" — "applicable to every available model".

Currently, users can only enable "Extended Thinking: Solve complex problems". These three new reasoning intensity/thinking levels will correspond to the options offered in Google AI Studio and Antigravity.

How Gemini 4 Argon will be positioned remains unclear. Google announced earlier this week that it would first be made available to AI Ultra subscribers. The company has not yet indicated whether Argon will be classified as a Pro model, or belong to a new tier above Pro.
